title: Profiling: getting to know the table before touching it

videos.script: Before you change a single value, you look. Not at ten rows. At every column, measured. {{look}} That is profiling. For each column, how many values are filled, how many are distinct, how short and how long they are, and which one turns up most. {{measures}} It sounds like bookkeeping. It is where the defects show themselves. A customer id that should be unique appears twice. A birth year is most often 1900. A total is negative. {{finds}} Then the shapes. Turn every digit into a nine and every letter into an a, and count what is left. A postcode column turns out to hold three formats. A date column holds two shapes and three meanings. {{patterns}} Before all of that comes the file itself. Its encoding, its separator, and what your tools guessed about it without asking. {{file}} By the end of this lesson you will have a profile of every table, written down, and a list of questions for the people who own the data. {{end}}
